title: Cryptoblabes gnidiella Millière (Pyralidae, Phycitinae): An Emerging Grapevine Pest in Greece
content: The honeydew moth, Cryptoblabes gnidiella Millière (Lepidoptera: Pyralidae), is native to the Mediterranean Basin. However, it has recently been reported as an emerging grapevine pest in southern European Union countries and in the Middle East, North Africa and South America. This may be attributed to the global warming trends. In this brief communication, we present the first documented cases of honeydew moth infestation of grapevine in Greece (Northeastern Greece 2024). We discuss the potential implications and concerns regarding the occurrence and management of this pest in Greece. Integrated pest management practices may contribute to reducing reliance on chemical pesticides and developing more sustainable approaches.
